title: EVE: evolutionary model predicts disease-variant pathogenicity without labels
summary: EVE, an unsupervised deep generative model trained on evolutionary sequence variation across about 140,000 species, predicted pathogenicity for more than 36 million variants in 3,219 disease genes and classified over 256,000 variants of unknown significance. The authors report it outperforms methods trained on labelled disease data and performs on par with high-throughput experimental predictions. Caveat: the authors state EVE is not a diagnostic test.
ai_technology: EVE (deep generative evolutionary model, variational autoencoder)
organization: University of Oxford; Harvard Medical School
